description: The pre-upload View Summary table: per-section record counts and CGST/SGST/IGST/cess totals, computed from the working payload (upload-JSON shape, validated rows only) and cached in a `_meta.json` sidecar next to the working file. Display-only — nothing here enters the upload file. Row order and the `name` labels are the official tool's, verbatim, typos included.

provenance.source: service/offline.js: reformSummary walks the payload and counts, generateTotal accumulates the four tax heads with the sign and zeroing rules, update_meta_file supplies the row list, labels and period gating; the base row list is public/data/tablename.json (GSTR1).

notes: The table has exactly six columns: section name, count (headed 'No. of Invoices' regardless of what one count actually is), total CGST, SGST, IGST and cess. Taxable value is NOT summed and has no column; neither do gross advances (ad_amt), invoice values (val) or quantities.

Rows with count 0 are omitted from the counts array itself (`if (count)`), not merely hidden. That same mechanism excludes `nil` and `doc_issue`: they are iterated but have no counting case, so their count stays 0 and they never appear. The page carries a disclaimer saying these two sections are not captured but still reach the generated file.

Each amount is rounded to two places before adding and the running total is re-rounded after every addition (parseFloat(toFixed(2))). All stored amounts are already two-place decimals, so exact decimal accumulation reproduces this.
An amount of 0 or a missing key contributes nothing; a genuinely negative stored amount flows through and reduces the total (JS truthiness guards the read, and negatives are truthy).

`count` is the path from each of a section's payload objects to the counted nodes; `amounts` continues from a counted node to each amount-bearing object. An empty path means the object itself. Array segments fan out; a missing segment contributes nothing.
Amount keys are camt/samt/iamt/csamt everywhere except supeco/supecoa, whose rows carry cgst/sgst/igst/cess instead — the per-row `amount_keys` maps the canonical column names to the payload keys.

`negate` subtracts instead of adds when the named field on the counted node takes one of the listed values: credit notes (C) and refund vouchers (R) reduce the totals, debit notes (D) add. The field sits on the note for cdnr/cdnra and on the record for cdnur/cdnura — both are the counted node, so one rule covers both.

`zero` blanks the listed columns (before accumulation) when the named field equals the given value; `at` says whether the field is read on the counted node or on the payload object (envelope). SEZ-without-payment, export-without-payment and unregistered-notes-against-export-without-payment supplies therefore show 0 IGST and 0 cess in the summary even though the stored items may carry tax.

The zero rules on the four ecom b2b-shaped sections are declared at the envelope because the reference reads inv_typ on the outer stin/rtin object — which never carries one, so the rule can never fire. Encoded for fidelity, not effect.

`from_period`/`until_period` gate a row by return period, matching update_meta_file's conditional appends and the HSN bifurcation. The merged `hsn` row (until 04-2025) is declared for fidelity, but this engine registers no merged hsn section, so it is inert.
Quarterly (TPQ) filers get a reduced e-commerce row set in non-quarter-end months; this engine models monthly filing only.

The meta file shape is {gstin, fp, version, hash, counts} — plus gt/cur_gt after fp when the working file carries turnover — where version and hash are the upload-envelope literals. Each counts entry is written in key order {cd, result, count, name}, and result in key order {cgTl, sgTl, igTl, csTl}.

reformSummary has payload-key fallbacks (atadj→txpd, cdnr→cdn, ecom*/ecoma* and hsn(...) all read one merged key) so it can also summarise a generated upload file. This engine keeps sections separate before enveloping, so no aliasing is needed here.
The four table-15 labels carry a NON-BREAKING SPACE (U+00A0) between '9(5)' and '- 15'; the 15A labels use a plain space. Invisible in the source, confirmed against a captured meta file.
